problems.description: Employees receive emails that appear to come from internal IT requesting credential updates. The messages contain malicious links that harvest login credentials when clicked.
risk_reduction: Enable multi‑factor authentication (MFA) for all user accounts
Deploy email filtering to flag or quarantine suspicious senders
Run regular security awareness training and phishing simulations

problems.description: The data represents a cybersecurity threat scenario where malicious actors use email communications to deliver phishing and spam content. Malicious emails often contain promotional or urgent language in the subject and body, including offers for financial gain, health products, or fraudulent business opportunities. These emails embed suspicious URLs and use formatting tricks such as reply prefixes and mailing list tags to appear legitimate. The benign emails contrast with neutral or technical language, often containing conversational or informational content without promotional intent. The threat exploits user trust in email communications to induce clicks on malicious links or engagement with fraudulent offers.
problems.asset_targeted: End Users (via deception to obtain sensitive information or induce action)

indicators_of_compromise: Subject lines with promotional or urgent language (e.g., 'Part-Time opportunity - $2000/week')
Presence of special characters, encoded content, and HTML-like tags in email bodies
Use of reply prefixes ('Re:'), mailing list tags (e.g., '[zzzzteana]') in subjects
Malicious emails often include calls to action or financial inducements
Sender/source labels associated with known malicious datasets (e.g., 'TREC-07', 'Enron')
attack_patterns: Use of persuasive language to lure recipients into clicking links or responding
Embedding URLs that lead to potentially harmful websites
Impersonation or spoofing tactics using familiar mailing list tags or reply formatting
Long, multi-paragraph email bodies with elaborate narratives to build trust
Inclusion of fake business or financial opportunity scenarios (e.g., inheritance scams)
normal_patterns: Neutral or technical language in subjects and bodies
Emails often structured as replies or discussions in mailing lists
Presence of legitimate email headers and formatting
Absence of promotional or urgent calls to action
Sources associated with benign datasets (e.g., 'Ling', 'TREC-07' with non-malicious content)

risk_reduction: Implement robust email filtering solutions that analyze subject and body content for promotional and suspicious language patterns
Deploy URL reputation and sandboxing technologies to detect and block malicious links
User awareness training to recognize phishing tactics and suspicious email characteristics
Use of sender authentication protocols such as SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to reduce spoofing
Monitor email source categories to identify and block high-risk origins
problems.data_source_notes: The dataset contains well-structured email samples with clear labeling (malicious=1, benign=0) and preserved schema reflecting realistic email subject and body patterns. The presence of known data sources such as 'TREC-07' and 'Enron' enhances reliability. Label distribution and content correlations align with expected phishing and benign email characteristics, supporting strong confidence in the analysis.

value_patterns: Short to medium length text strings
Includes alphanumeric characters, punctuation, and special characters
Typical length ranges from a few words to about 10-15 words
May include email or group references in brackets

constraints.format_pattern: Free text with optional mailing list tags or reply prefixes

subject.generation_instructions: Generate varied text strings resembling email subjects, optionally including reply prefixes ('Re:'), mailing list tags in brackets (e.g., '[zzzzteana]'), and typical punctuation. Length should be roughly 5-15 words. Include alphanumeric and special characters as in real email subjects.
subject.relationship_to_label: Malicious subjects often contain promotional or urgent language (e.g., 'Guaranteed to lose 10-12 lbs', 'Life Insurance - Why Pay More?'), while benign subjects tend to be more neutral or technical (e.g., 'Re: New Sequences Window').

value_patterns: Contains email headers, URLs, special characters, and line breaks
May include HTML-like tags or encoded characters
Includes natural language text with punctuation and formatting
Length varies widely, from short messages to very long emails

constraints.format_pattern: Free text email body with possible embedded URLs, headers, and encoded characters

body.generation_instructions: Generate multi-sentence paragraphs resembling email bodies. Include realistic email formatting such as headers (Date, From, Message-ID), URLs, line breaks, and occasional encoded or special characters. Malicious bodies often contain promotional content, offers, or calls to action; benign bodies are more conversational or technical.
body.relationship_to_label: Malicious bodies frequently contain marketing language, discount offers, or suspicious links. Benign bodies are more likely to contain technical discussions, replies, or neutral content.

label.generation_instructions: Assign label 1 for malicious samples and 0 for benign samples exactly as per original encoding.
label.relationship_to_label: Target variable indicating malicious (1) or benign (0) email.

value_patterns: Limited set of unique values (5 unique)

allowed_values: Other possible source values as per original dataset

source.generation_instructions: Randomly assign one of the original source categories, preserving the original distribution if known. Use exact string values as in the original data.
source.relationship_to_label: Source may correlate with label distribution; some sources may have higher malicious content.

value_generation_strategy.malicious_samples: Generate 'subject' and 'body' text with promotional, urgent, or marketing language patterns. Include URLs, special characters, and formatting typical of spam/phishing emails. Assign label=1 and sample 'source' from categories associated with malicious data.
value_generation_strategy.benign_samples: Generate 'subject' and 'body' text with neutral, technical, or conversational language. Include email headers and typical mailing list or reply formatting. Assign label=0 and sample 'source' from categories associated with benign data.

quality_checks: Verify column names and order exactly match ['subject', 'body', 'label', 'source']
Ensure data types match: 'subject' and 'body' as object (string), 'label' as int64 with values 0 or 1, 'source' as object with allowed categories
Check no unexpected nulls beyond original counts (subject nulls ≤ 753, body nulls ≤ 1, label and source no nulls)
Validate label encoding strictly limited to 0 and 1
Confirm 'source' values are only from original set of 5 unique strings
Ensure generated text fields follow length and pattern distributions similar to original samples
Maintain approximate label distribution ratio (~51% malicious, ~49% benign)
Cross-check correlations: promotional language in 'subject' and 'body' aligns with label=1, neutral language aligns with label=0
